newsitem.title: GERMANY: No decision on extra '97 borrowing-German FinMin.
newsitem.headline: No decision on extra '97 borrowing-German FinMin.

text.p: No decision has been taken on the amount of extra borrowing in the supplementary budget for 1997 announced by the German government on Friday, a spokesman for the Finance Ministry said.

"No decision has yet been taken on the scale and timing," the spokesman said when asked how much extra borrowing was envisaged in the supplementary budget announced earlier by Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl.
Bohl said in a statement earlier that Bonn would draft a supplementary budget which would make "an exceptional allowance for higher new borrowing".

Bonn earlier this year raised its budget deficit target for 1997 from an originally budgeted 2.5 percent to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product -- just shy of the three percent ceiling specified by the Maastricht treaty.

The spokesman declined to say whether the higher borrowing would take Germany's combined public sector deficit over the strict target of exactly 3.0 percent which Finance Minister Theo Waigel has in the past pledged to meet.
He noted that the Maastricht treaty only mentioned the figure "three", and added: "The government will do everything possible to achieve that."
The supplementary budget became necessary after German unemployment overshot official projections and tax revenue estimates last month fell short of target, the spokesman said.
